claims.claim: NVIDIA released the Personal AI Router (PAIR) as an open-source software project under the Apache 2.0 license on GitHub.
PAIR functions as a local inference router and load balancer that automatically discovers available computing nodes across a local network using mDNS.
claims.notes: Routes multi-agent inference requests across LAN nodes.

claims.claim: PAIR supports NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20-series GPUs and newer, NVIDIA RTX PRO workstation GPUs, DGX Spark, and Apple Silicon M4+ devices.
claims.notes: Broad hardware coverage across Windows, Linux, and macOS.

claims.claim: PAIR integrates with Ollama and LM Studio by providing OpenAI-compatible and Ollama-compatible proxy endpoints.
claims.notes: Enables existing multi-agent frameworks to plug in without modifications.

claims.claim: PAIR does not pool VRAM, combine GPUs into a single virtual accelerator, or shard single models; it routes independent, discrete inference requests.
claims.notes: CRITICAL BOUNDARY: Clarify that PAIR is a query load balancer, not a tensor-parallel model sharding system.

claims.claim: All model execution and agent communications routed through PAIR remain entirely on the local area network with zero data sent to external cloud servers.

sources.name: NVIDIA Personal AI Router GitHub Repository

editorial_cautions: Emphasize that PAIR routes individual discrete requests and does NOT merge GPU VRAM or split single models across nodes.
Highlight cross-platform support including Apple Silicon alongside RTX hardware.
